value.rationale: The affine isotropic constant is a natural shape descriptor in convex geometry, and regular Reuleaux odd-gons form the canonical order-indexed constant-width family approaching a disk. The known raw area and inertia defects both begin at n^-2 but cancel after normalization, so neither fixed-order formula nor easy separate monotonicities resolve the cross-order behavior. The proved strict order is a genuine infinite classification and makes the invariant identify odd n uniquely; its exact adjacent-order n^-5 separation quantifies conditioning. The sign requires a nontrivial uniform rational certificate rather than a few finite evaluations. No unrestricted constant-width optimization is claimed.
